answer: Quadratic staking forces each validator to lock collateral scaling as the square of its stake, while a zero-knowledge verifiable delay reveals misbehavior after a fixed epoch and imposes an ember penalty that aggregates into a karst of unrecoverable loss. The resulting super-linear marginal attack cost outpaces any extractable reward, yielding negative expected utility and a crystal Nash equilibrium that secures consensus. Liquidity-sink commitments further raise coordinated exit costs, cementing protocol resilience.
